Congonhas is one of the stops on historical routes through the state of Minas Gerais. The city is associated with the gold-mining era, when settlements with stone streets, churches and tiled-roof houses grew up in Brazil's interior. Its architecture and religious art reveal a different side of the country, far from the beach resorts.

The main attraction in Congonhas is its historic religious complex and sculptural heritage. A walk around the city fits naturally into a trip that also includes Ouro Preto and Mariana. Here, it is worth slowing down to appreciate the details of the old buildings and the rolling landscape of Minas Gerais.

Copacabana stands on the Bolivian shore of Lake Titicaca. Travellers arrive here from La Paz across the Altiplano plateau.

From the town, the journey continues by boat to the Island of the Sun. In this way, Copacabana links the overland part of a trip through Bolivia with an excursion on the lake and an introduction to Inca heritage.

Coquesa, a village near the Uyuni Salt Flat, is a stop on routes through high-altitude Bolivia. Travellers combine a visit here with an introduction to the area's mountain and salt-flat landscapes.

The itinerary offers a chance to see settlements beside the salt flat. The nature of the walk and the onward route depend on the tour selected.

The railway ascent introduces visitors to the city's greener side. The trees of Tijuca Forest pass by the windows before the summit opens up. The statue of Christ the Redeemer, erected in 1931, has become one of Rio's most recognisable symbols.

Corcovado rises to approximately 700 metres above sea level. From beside the statue, visitors can take in views of Guanabara Bay, Sugarloaf Mountain and the densely built-up city. Visibility depends on the cloud cover: clear skies reveal more details, while mist can quickly change the experience at the summit.

A visit to Corcovado is often combined with a sightseeing tour of Rio. When planning the excursion, it is important to consider both the means of ascent and the language of the guide; the train and road options are different ways of reaching the viewpoint.

Corcovado is located in southern Costa Rica and protects tropical natural habitats. Here, the forest meets the Pacific Ocean, so exploring the park can combine rainforest trails with stretches of coastline. One well-known area for walking is near the Sirena Ranger Station.

Nature trails offer an introduction to the plants and animals of the rainforest. Reaching some parts of the park involves a boat journey along the coast, which also provides a view of the park from the water. Corcovado reveals southern Costa Rica through its forests, rivers and coastal landscapes.
